Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 19/2021); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 973/2021, de 9 de noviembre, regulador de la declaración de titularidad real (Registro de Titularidades Reales, RTR); Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a emprendedores; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC). UBO identification is also integrated through the Registro Mercantil Central and notarial protocols under the framework of Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A fully virtual office with no physical desk sharing is not generally accepted for initial incorporation of an SL under mandatory requirements in Law 14/2013 and the Ley de Sociedades de Capital. However, Spanish commercial law permits a registered office to be any place within Spanish territory, and 'virtual office' service providers in Spain (including Madrid and Barcelona) are accepted if they provide a physical address with a mailbox and a real reception facility for invoicing and official notifications. For an AI/BPO business engaged solely in data labeling with no public-facing physical presence, a registered agent service with a physical office location and mail forwarding is permissible, but the tax authorities (AEAT) and the Commercial Registry may require proof of commensurate commercial substance, generally the retention of a leased office space or an identifiable workplace for employees/contractors. A phased arrangement using a reputable corporate service provider's physical address is accepted during pre-incorporation and for the first 6 months, after which a physical place of operations must be evidenced.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation certificate) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid); deed executed before a Spanish Notary for the province of the registered office.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Articles 4 (minimum capital), 20-22 (public deed and commercial registration), 62 (sole administrator) and 102-104 (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada); modified by Ley 18/2022 de Creación y Crecimiento de Empresas; notarial formalities under Ley 6/2014 del Notariado.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public deed of incorporation incorporating the Estatutos Sociales or Articles of Association).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 45 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Default statutory minimum under Article 4 LSC is 3,000 EUR fully subscribed and fully paid-up in cash or kind; alternatively, under Ley 18/2022, capital may be fixed at 1 EUR provided full discharge in cash, mandatory legal reserve until reaching 3,000 EUR, and solvency conditions per Article 4.2 LSC. The paid-up amount must be evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit (certificado bancario de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution; non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report under Article 67 LSC.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate per RD 513/2017 (RSCIEI) and Código Técnico de la Edificación DB-SI: fire doors, automatic detection, extinguishers at 15m spacing, emergency lighting and evacuation signage; structural load inspection certificate per CTE for office loading; occupational risk prevention workplace health and safety assessment per Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales and RD 171/2004; low-voltage electrical installation certificate per RD 842/2002; first-aid equipment, workplace signage and emergency plan prepared by the preventive organisation; employer registration with an accredited PRL service where workforce exceeds six employees.

Paid-in capital rule: Default statutory minimum under Article 4 LSC is 3,000 EUR fully subscribed and fully paid-up in cash or kind; alternatively, under Ley 18/2022, capital may be fixed at 1 EUR provided full discharge in cash, mandatory legal reserve until reaching 3,000 EUR, and solvency conditions per Article 4.2 LSC. The paid-up amount must be evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit (certificado bancario de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution; non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report under Article 67 LSC.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
FIRST: All shares issued in the incorporation deed are subscribed and accepted; the paid-up capital of 3,000 EUR (or 1 EUR under the Crea y Crece regime, subject to the statutory reserve) is acknowledged as fully discharged. SECOND: The registered office for statutory, tax and administrative purposes is fixed at [address], Madrid, within the province of Madrid; relocation within the same municipality is delegated to the administrator. THIRD: [Name] is appointed sole administrator (administrador único), exercising all powers of representation with legal limitation of liability. FOURTH: The administrator is mandated to execute all notarial, registry, tax, labour and banking formalities required for incorporation and registration.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Agricultura y Vivienda of the competent Comunidad Autónoma (Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental) and the municipal licensing authority of the registered office (e.g., Dirección General de Licencias del Ayuntamiento de Madrid).

Category: Licencia Urbanística de Actividad / Municipal Activity Licence, or Declaración Responsable de Apertura de Establecimiento where the premises are low-impact and under the thresholds of Ley 12/2012 and the municipal ordinance.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - www.agenciatributaria.es

E-government filing portal

For a non-resident-owned Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) Obtain an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) for the foreign legal representative via the Spanish consulate or the Oficina de Extranjería; (2) Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary and file it with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); (3) Apply for the provisional NIF/CIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the company by filing Modelo 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of incorporation; (4) Register the company in the IVA census (Censo de Obligados Tributarios); (5) For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment that is a direct supplier or service recipient, obtain a NIF-N (entity NIF for non-residents) using Modelo 036/030. The definitive NIF is issued subsequent to the registration of the deed; the SL itself is a resident tax entity always subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — For a non-resident-owned Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) Obtain an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) for the foreign legal representative via the Spanish consulate or the Oficina de Extranjería; (2) Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary and file it with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); (3) Apply for the provisional NIF/CIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the company by filing Modelo 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of incorporation; (4) Register the company in the IVA census (Censo de Obligados Tributarios); (5) For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment that is a direct supplier or service recipient, obtain a NIF-N (entity NIF for non-residents) using Modelo 036/030. The definitive NIF is issued subsequent to the registration of the deed; the SL itself is a resident tax entity always subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No check-the-box regime exists; the SL is statutorily a separate taxable entity subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS). Available elections include: (i) optional cash-basis IVA (criterio de caja) for SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 2,000,000; (ii) voluntary enrollment in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) for electronic VAT reporting; (iii) tax consolidation regime (régimen de grupos fiscales) for groups meeting the 75% ownership threshold under Articles 58-64 Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; (iv) the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive hybrid mismatch disclosures/modeling elections under Article 15 bis LGT and related IS rules. No US-style classification election is applicable; non-resident shareholders do not alter the Spanish entity-level taxation default.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

Spain does not operate a general economic turnover exemption threshold analogous to the UK VAT threshold. Any entity performing taxable economic activities within Spanish territory (peninsula, Balearic Islands) is compulsorily required to register in the IVA census prior to commencing activity, irrespective of projected turnover. A reduced-regime threshold applies only for the special simplified schemes (régimen simplificado), which AI/BPO services are not eligible for; the optional cash-basis IVA regime (criterio de caja) is available for taxpayers with annual turnover below EUR 2,000,000. The SII real-time reporting obligation is mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

For services (including computer vision annotation and RLHF data curation BPO): zero-ratd/outside-scope treatment under Article 69.Uno and Article 70.1.2º LIVA applies where the recipient is a taxable person (empresario o profesional) established in another EU Member State or in a third country, provided the effective use and exploitation of the AI data labeling services occurs outside the Spanish IVA territory. The transaction is then taxed under the reverse-charge mechanism at destination (0% in Spain). For B2C supplies to non-EU customers, the 'use and enjoyment' place-of-supply rules may keep the services within Spanish IVA where the tangible work product (e.g., annotated datasets) is physically deployed in Spain; therefore, the BPO must document end-customer establishment and actual use. For goods exports (not the typical BPO model but applicable to any physical data storage devices containing deliverable datasets), a 0% rate applies under Article 21 LIVA where goods are dispatched outside the EU within 3 months, evidenced by the electronic customs declaration (DEX).

  • Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo/DUA - DEX) registered in the aduana with electronic data interchange; required for physical goods dispatching (including GPU servers or data-storage devices) outside the EU
  • Bill of Lading or Airway Bill in the exporter's name evidencing dispatch to the non-EU customer's location
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence of collection of export consideration into a Spanish bank account in the company's name
  • Service Agreement and Work Order between ES_SL and the foreign client stating the nature of the AI data labeling services, the place of supply, and customer's identity
  • Proof of customer's foreign taxable-person status (EU VAT registration number validated via VIES, or foreign business registration certificate / TIN from the non-EU jurisdiction)
  • Signed certificate of service delivery and, where applicable, digital acceptance receipt from the offshore client evidencing that the labeled datasets were used/exploited outside Spain
  • Internal costing and transfer pricing file if the BPO is performed at arm's length (Chapter IV documentation) supporting the commercial rationale of the export flow

Under Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece', all entrepreneurs and professionals must issue, deliver and receive electronic invoices (Facturae format or equivalent structured/XML format) in their B2B relationships. Mandatory phasing: businesses with annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000 must comply within one year of the enabling regulation; all remaining businesses within two years. Invoice issuance must incorporate the standard Spanish obligatory invoice data fields (Serie, NIF del emisor y receptor, Base Imponible, Tipo impositivo, Cuota). For IVA purposes, all invoice data, including customer VAT identification, must be transmitted to AEAT either through the SII real-time fiscal clearance system (mandatory for turnover > EUR 6,000,000; voluntary for others) or through the annual recapitulative statements (Modelo 347/349 for intra-EU supplies). No physical tax stamp is required on invoices; the fiscal clearance is electronic. SII mandates XML structured transmission (Web Service API at https://www.agenciatributaria.es) to AEAT within 4 calendar days of invoice issuance.

False or insufficiently documented zero-rating claims are treated as undue tax advantage. AEAT may lawfully deviate the IVA and impose: (i) the difference between the 21% IVA incorrectly omitted and the 0% claim, as tax debt (cuota); (ii) late-payment interest (interés de demora) calculated from the end of the voluntary payment period of the tax period; (iii) a proportional penalty for tax infractions under Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria Article 191, typically 50% to 100% of the cuota, with reduction to 25%/50% where the adjustment is conformed voluntarily; (iv) where fraudulent intent (ánimo de defraudar) is shown, penalties of up to 150% of the cuota, and criminal referral under Articles 305/305 bis Código Penal for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000; (v) denial of refund or re-credit of IVA previously reclaimed in Modelo 303/390 filings, plus derogation for up to six months to model the correct IVA position. In SII compliance audits, failure to file the export-supporting documentation digitally within four days may additionally trigger an Article 203 LGT penalty of EUR 200 per invoice, and non-cooperation in audit procedures (obstrucción) may attract EUR 600.00 to EUR 6,000.00 penalties. Retrospective clawback is generally possible for up to four years from the invoice issuance date (statute of limitations), extended by the fraud limitation rule to ten years in criminal cases.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain maintains full capital account convertibility and current account convertibility under EU acquis and Spanish law. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted and freely convertible without prior regulatory approval, subject only to standard AML/KYC screening and tax compliance filings with the AEAT.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds applies in Spain or the EU. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts and converted at market rates. All export transactions require statistical declaration to the Spanish Customs Agency (AEAT) via the TRACES system; banks may request supporting invoices and contracts for transactions exceeding reporting thresholds.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

PayPal Fit: High

High feasibility for offshore digital EMIs via licensed platforms such as Wise and PayPal. Legal constraints include mandatory compliance with Spanish Payment Services Directive (PSD2) requirements, Bank of Spain registration for payment institutions, and full AML/KYC verification of the SL entity.

Wise Fit: High

High feasibility for offshore digital EMIs via licensed platforms such as Wise and PayPal. Legal constraints include mandatory compliance with Spanish Payment Services Directive (PSD2) requirements, Bank of Spain registration for payment institutions, and full AML/KYC verification of the SL entity.

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: An independent statutory audit is generally required when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: EUR 4 million total assets, EUR 8 million net annual turnover, or 50 average employees. Mandatory audit also applies to certain regulated or public-interest entities and other cases prescribed by law.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Qualifying EU or EEA parent companies may obtain full exemption under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive where ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 5%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty and ownership percentage.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the usual filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing deadline is extended under the AEAT calendar rules.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December. The December installment is normally due from 1 to 20 December. Large companies subject to the alternative tax-base method may have additional calculation requirements. The final corporate tax liability is settled through Modelo 200.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the usual deadline is 30 November of the following year.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File documentation is generally required for controlled transactions with the same related person or entity exceeding EUR 250,000 in the relevant transaction category during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and special rules. Master File documentation is generally required for Spanish entities forming part of a multinational group where consolidated group turnover is at least EUR 750 million. Country-by-country reporting generally applies at the EUR 750 million consolidated group-revenue threshold and is normally filed by the reporting entity in the relevant jurisdiction, with Spanish notification obligations where applicable.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Nevertheless, Spanish tax law requires genuine economic activity, arm's-length conduct, beneficial ownership, and business purpose. The tax authorities may apply the general anti-abuse rule, simulation doctrine, recharacterization, transfer-pricing rules, controlled-foreign-company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest-limitation rules, principal-purpose tests, and EU anti-abuse principles. A Spanish SL performing data labeling or AI-training BPO should maintain Spanish personnel or demonstrable operational capacity, premises or documented remote-work infrastructure, decision-making evidence, customer contracts, time records, service deliverables, cybersecurity controls, and commercially rational pricing.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion and Fraud

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, in addition to tax and interest. Where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 for a tax period, the conduct may constitute a criminal tax offense punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized fraud, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and higher fines.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability, subsidiary tax liability, administrative sanctions, and criminal liability where they participated in or knowingly enabled the conduct. Courts may impose asset seizure, disqualification, and travel restrictions where legally justified; travel bans are not automatic.
False Invoicing and VAT Fraud

Statutory sanction: VAT assessments, repayment of improperly claimed input tax, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties generally calculated as a percentage of the improperly deducted or unpaid tax. Serious or organized conduct may constitute a tax or accounting crime under the Criminal Code.

Director personal liability: Directors who approve fictitious invoices or knowingly sign false tax returns may face joint civil restitution, subsidiary tax liability, criminal prosecution, asset seizure, professional disqualification, and imprisonment where criminal thresholds are met.
Transfer-Pricing Manipulation

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment to arm's-length income, deny unsupported deductions, impose secondary adjustments, assess interest, and apply transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Failure to document or materially misreporting controlled transactions can generate fixed or transaction-linked penalties under Spanish tax law.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability for tax losses caused by knowingly unsupported related-party arrangements and criminal exposure if the adjustment forms part of deliberate tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold.
Beneficial-Ownership and Treaty Abuse

Statutory sanction: Denial of exemption or treaty reduction, assessment of unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Anti-abuse rules may recharacterize the arrangement and impose withholding at the domestic rate.

Director personal liability: Directors approving knowingly false beneficial-owner representations may incur withholding-tax liability, civil restitution, administrative penalties, and criminal liability for document fraud or tax fraud.
Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may disregard artificial arrangements, deny deductions and exemptions, recharacterize transactions, impose tax and interest, and apply the general anti-abuse rule. Criminal consequences may arise if the structure facilitates tax fraud, money laundering, or falsification.

Director personal liability: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil liability, tax-liability derivation, asset freezing, disqualification, and criminal prosecution. Corporate personality is not automatically disregarded, but veil piercing may occur in cases of fraud, abuse, commingling, or unlawful evasion.
Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist-Financing Breach

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish Law 10/2010, serious and very serious AML infringements may result in public or private reprimands, temporary suspension, and fines that can reach EUR 1.5 million, 5% of the net worth of the obligated person, or up to ten times the value of the transaction or benefit, subject to the applicable classification and statutory limits.

Director personal liability: Managers and directors may be personally sanctioned where the infringement is attributable to them. Criminal money-laundering liability may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and disqualification. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court when necessary for criminal proceedings.
Accounting, Corporate-Book, and Annual-Accounts Failure

Statutory sanction: Corporate, accounting, commercial-register, and tax consequences may include fines, refusal or delay of registry filings, administrative tax adjustments, audit qualifications, and criminal accounting liability where the conduct causes material deception or supports fraud.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur liability for losses caused to the company, shareholders, creditors, or the tax authority, and may face disqualification, civil restitution, or criminal sanctions for deliberate falsification.
Payroll, Social-Security, and Worker Misclassification

Statutory sanction: Back assessments, social-security contributions, surcharges, employment-tax interest, labor fines, and potentially criminal sanctions may apply. The exact amount depends on the period, number of workers, concealment, and severity.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur subsidiary liability for unpaid social-security obligations and withholding taxes, civil claims from workers, labor sanctions, and criminal liability in aggravated cases.
Data Protection, Confidentiality, and AI-Training Misuse

Statutory sanction: The Spanish Data Protection Agency may impose GDPR administrative fines of up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for the relevant infringement category, in addition to corrective orders, processing bans, and contractual damages.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil and, in exceptional cases, criminal liability for unlawful disclosure, secrecy breaches, or intentional misuse. GDPR fines are generally imposed on the company, but individual liability may arise under separate civil or criminal provisions.
Payment-Services and Unauthorized Financial Activity

Statutory sanction: Regulatory orders, account suspension, repayment obligations, administrative fines, and potential criminal consequences may apply depending on whether the conduct constitutes unauthorized payment services, fraud, or money laundering.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for knowingly operating unauthorized financial services, misleading banks or payment institutions, or facilitating illicit funds. Asset seizure and travel restrictions may be ordered in criminal proceedings.
